    process/composition columns (Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, Mn, C, Ti, Si, Nb, V, P, B,

    cooling rate, Heat treatment step 2 temperature, Heat treatment step 2 time, Heat treatment step 2

  - b3_htsteel_process_pool.csv: 34 CANDIDATE samples whose yield strength
    at room temperature (MPa) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST yield
strength at room temperature (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from
the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I would prioritize candidates tempered at **200–450°C after the 1050°C first heat-treatment stage**, without subsequent long-duration aging.

The training data support this selection:
- In the **13% Cr, 0.12% C** family, a 250°C second-stage treatment gives **930 MPa**, compared with **780 MPa** at 540°C.
- Related **11.25% Cr martensitic steels** reach **1,330–1,340 MPa** with 200–400°C second-stage treatments, versus approximately **750–910 MPa** at 600–650°C.
- The pool candidates treated at 715–740°C are closer to substantially lower-strength training examples. Subsequent aging does not reliably recover that strength.

My predicted ranking is:

| Rank | Candidate | Heat treatment step 2 temperature |
|---:|---|---:|
| 1 | **c006** | 450°C |
| 2 | **c014** | 450°C |
| 3 | **c017** | 300°C |
| 4 | **c018** | 300°C |
| 5 | **c021** | 200°C |

The precise ordering is uncertain: the training set does not contain this exact 0.20% C composition across all these tempering temperatures. The strongest conclusion is that this low-temperature-treatment group should outperform the high-temperature-tempered and extensively aged alternatives.

Final: c006, c014, c017, c018, c021
